request.spec:
A steward can transfer a person to another sheet by id (an entry and a button on the row; anyone
else, a retired person, this sheet's own id, is refused with an error on the row). The person
arrives on the other sheet with every grade they were given (and its from-date), their terms,
contact, aliases and tags, and their claims with their status, dates, notes, frozen figures and
logs; each claim that had a number receives the next number of the other sheet, in the order the
claims were opened (by the sheet's today when each was opened, then by the order they were added);
figures a statement bound are lost and the statement count starts at 0; references are not carried.
A name, alias or contact already on the other sheet refuses the transfer. The person leaves this
sheet entirely (patron links, pool memberships, plans and watches dropped). This sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> to=<sheet id>, the other PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet
id>, each followed by that sheet's rollup lines.

A name, alias or contact already on the other sheet refuses the transfer. The person leaves this

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: A background wait I'd started was stopped when it hit its time limit. It was only polling for the first test run to finish, and it never exited because its own command line contained "playwright test", the text it was searching for. Nothing depended on it: I'd already read that run's results, and the later full run is the one I reported. That run still stands: the transfer test passes, and scenarios 2 and 3 fail on the consolidated panel, as they did before my change.
